claim.purpose: Make terminal projection and retained receipt updates crash-consistent

initial.title: [v0.91.8][csdlc-v2][durability] Make terminal projection and receipt crash-consistent
initial.goal: Make terminal projection and retained receipt updates crash-consistent and recoverable.
initial.required_outcome: A terminal reconciliation either durably commits both projection and receipt or leaves a journaled state that deterministically recovers without generation or identity drift.
authority_boundary: The Rust v2 store and receipt journal are the sole durability authority
Existing terminal receipt identity, rollback, idempotence, and typed reconciliation contracts remain unchanged
initial.task_boundary: Add a bounded journaled terminal projection/receipt transaction with deterministic recovery and fault-injection proof.
deliverables: Crash-consistent terminal transaction or recovery journal
acceptance_criteria: Projection and receipt converge to one generation after success or recovery
Receipt bytes and parent directory are synchronized before success
Interruption before and after each durable write/rename recovers deterministically
Identity, rollback, idempotence, and typed reconciliation contracts remain green
dependencies: Rust filesystem primitives and focused test harness
initial.plan_summary: Map the existing projection/receipt writes, introduce a journal and fsync boundaries, inject interruption at every commit point, then prove deterministic recovery and idempotence.

steps.action: Map terminal projection, receipt, journal, and recovery boundaries
Implement synchronized journaled commit and deterministic recovery
Run fault-injection, rollback, idempotence, and contract validation

invariants: Projection and receipt share one canonical generation and digest
No successful return occurs before receipt bytes and parent directory are synchronized
Existing receipt identity and rollback semantics are preserved
risks: Filesystem synchronization semantics differ across supported hosts
Fault injection must not weaken normal lifecycle locking or receipt retention
stop_conditions: Every durable write/rename interruption point has deterministic recovery proof
Focused durability and lifecycle checks are green
Subagent review has no actionable findings
initial.failure_policy: Fail closed on ambiguous durability or recovery state; never report terminal success with unmatched projection and receipt.
review_prompts: Can interruption at every write/rename boundary recover deterministically?
Are receipt bytes and parent-directory metadata synchronized before success?
Are identity, rollback, and idempotence preserved?
Does the test harness prove both pre- and post-write interruption paths?
